detail:
The source compares mitochondria to rechargeable batteries that have to be recharged. He describes natural approaches — grounding, sunlight, minerals, and other natural processes — as a slower recharge, and presents frequency-specific microcurrent as the faster clinical option for people with chronic illness or autoimmune disease whose energy is "running on empty."

The source's own note: "For educational purposes only. Not medical advice."

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material.
sourceVideoTitle: Think of your mitochondria like a battery, they have to be recharged....
summary: The source compares mitochondria to rechargeable batteries and discusses natural and clinical ways to recharge them.
takeaways: Grounding — the source describes barefoot contact with the earth as a slow way to recharge.
Sunlight — also described by the source as a slower, natural recharge.
Minerals — named by the source as part of the natural recharge picture.
Frequency-specific microcurrent — the clinical option the source discusses for chronic illness and autoimmune conditions; talk to your doctor first.
title: Recharging cellular energy (mitochondria)
